newsitem.title: POLAND: Credit Lyonnais may buy Polish bank - paper.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais may buy Polish bank - paper.

text.p: France's Credit Lyonnais wants to buy a mid-sized Polish IBP Bank SA, in which it presently has a 27 percent stake, the Rzeczpospolita business daily reported on Monday.

The paper quoted unnamed sources as saying the French bank was in negotiations with Italy's Commit Holding International, a part of the Banca Commerciale Italiana Group, about purchasing its 27 percent stake in IBP.
Rzeczpospolita said that once Credit Lyonnais bought out Commit Holding and had a majority in IBP, it would likely offer to buy the remaining shares from other shareholders.
The paper said the remaining 46 percent stake would likely cost Credit Lyonnais about 150 million zlotys ($47.4 million).
Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy and Bank Rozwoju Eksportu both have a 15 percent stake in IBP and 16 percent is owned by the International Finance Corporation.

IBP deputy president Janusz Czarzasty said he did not know if any deal with Credit Lyonnais was in the works, but added that he did not have to be informed abot negotiations between individual shareholders.
"Credit Lyonnais had good results in the Central European region last year but this does not mean that they will buy IBP," Czarzasty told Reuters.
At the end of 1996 IBP had a 13.2 million zloty net profit, its own funds amounted to 98.9 million zlotys and assets were worth 526.1 million.
IBP is the 31st largest Polish bank in terms of assets and 26th largest in terms of own funds.
